page: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8280M cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz and includes 38 MB of L3 cache. The server is equipped with 219.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 54.69 GB per core. Local storage consists of 262 GB, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the M8-4ms prioritizes memory capacity over raw compute performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score is 1035.08, and the multi-core score is 2724.76, both falling into the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block speed of 151.25 GB/sec and a large block write speed of 17.19 GB/sec. Geekbench scores reflect similar constraints, with a single-core score of 885.0 and a multi-core score of 1970.0. Redis SET operations achieve 2.63 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 3.0 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a specialized trade-off, offering massive memory density per vCPU rather than high-performance compute resources. This makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require intense CPU processing, such as large in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications with massive memory footprints but moderate computational demands.
description: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for workloads requiring massive memory capacity relative to compute resources. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores) running at 2.7 GHz, the instance features 219.0 GB of RAM, providing 54.69 GB of memory per core. It includes 262 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, with no GPU acceleration. Benchmark data indicates modest compute and memory bandwidth performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1970.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 2724.76. Consequently, this server is best suited for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, and databases where memory capacity is the primary bottleneck rather than raw CPU throughput.
